rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

implementationCorrectness.description: Does the code do exactly what the change claims (its title and description when given, otherwise its code, comments and tests), handling edge cases and error paths without regressions? Score 1: logic is broken or contradicts what the change claims, misses an obvious edge case or error path, or silently regresses existing behavior. Score 10: matches what the change claims on the happy path, edge cases and failure modes, with no regressions; errors are reported, not swallowed.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

idiomaticity.description: Does the code read as if written by someone fluent in the language, the framework and this repository? Score 1: fights the idioms of the stack and the patterns of the repository; naming, structure and error handling are foreign to the surrounding code. Score 10: indistinguishable from well-written surrounding code; reuses existing helpers and conventions instead of duplicating them.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

complexity.description: Is the solution as simple as the problem allows? Score 1: over-engineered or tangled: needless abstractions, layers, flags or state that obscure intent. Score 10: minimal and clear; the simplest design that solves the whole problem, with nothing added for hypothetical future needs.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

testRiskCoverage.description: Are the meaningful behaviors and risky paths exercised by tests in proportion to their risk? Score 1: risky logic ships untested; tests are absent, trivial or assert nothing useful, or changed logic comes with no changed tests. Score 10: risk-weighted coverage; the parts most likely to break are tested deliberately, including the negative case.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

documentation.description: Are non-obvious decisions and public surfaces explained where a reader would need it? Score 1: intent must be reverse-engineered: no comment on a non-obvious choice, no docs for a public API, or public behavior changes with no matching doc change. Score 10: just enough to explain the why, without restating the obvious; comments and docs agree with the code.

rationale.description: Why this score was given: concrete findings with file paths and lines.

securitySafety.description: Does the change avoid introducing vulnerabilities, leaking secrets or handling untrusted input unsafely? Score 1: introduces an exploitable flaw such as injection, path traversal or a missing authorization check, logs or commits a secret, or trusts untrusted input. Score 10: input is validated at the boundary, secrets stay out of code and logs, and no new attack surface is opened, including dependencies the change does not need.

verdict.description: Binding verdict for the whole change; the CI gate reads only this field. Return fail if implementationCorrectness <= 5, or securitySafety <= 4, or any criterion <= 3; otherwise return pass.

summary.description: Markdown summary for a pull request comment: lead with the verdict, then the most important findings.
